newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-COMMISSION CALLS FOR SPORTS CHIEF TO BE SACKED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COMMISSION CALLS FOR SPORTS CHIEF TO BE SACKED.

text.p: A state-appointed commission has called for the resignation of South African Football Association (SAFA) president Solomon Morewa, Sports Minister Steve Tshwete said on Tuesday.
"The commission has called upon Mr Morewa to resign or be dismissed," Tshwete told a news conference.

He said the commission also found that an Irish-registered marketing company, Awesome Sports International (ASI), had "emasculated South African football" to the extent that it was no longer being run by SAFA.
Tshwete said SAFA had been given 21 days to react to the findings of the commission, which sat from May to December last year after prolonged press criticism of the way soccer was being run.
Morewa, who was accused of acting under the control of ASI and against the interests of SAFA, has admitted to receiving an interest-free "loan" of 500,000 rand ($106,000) from ASI in June 1994.
He also admitted awarding himself a bursary from a fund set up by SAFA to help players pay for education.

The commission also heard allegations that Morewa and powerful Kaizer Chiefs managing director Kaizer Motaung had led a troika of friends -- known as a the "A-team" -- in using soccer for personal gain.
During the sittings Judge Benjamin Pickard described the relationship between Morewa, ASI's Brian Mahon and Motaung as "unhealthy".
"Once Mr Morewa has been removed, the hold of ASI will be weakened and football should be allowed to normalise itself. You cannot be boss and employee," Tshwete said.

Morewa, who has been head of South African soccer since its international return four years ago said: "I'm shocked. This report is amazing. It's not the Pickard Commission, it's the Morewa Commission.
"Clearly it was my head they were looking for and I can't believe they're doing it now when the national side has won the African Nations Cup and is on course for the World Cup in France."
